definitions.definition: (of people and some animals) to move along, faster than walking, by taking quick steps in which each foot is lifted before the next foot touches the ground
definitions.example: [ + to infinitive ] The children had to run to keep up with their father.

definitions.definition: If you run an animal in a race, you cause it to take part
definitions.example: run something in something Thompson Stables are running three horses in the next race.

definitions.definition: to go quickly or in a hurry
definitions.example: Would you run to the post office and get me some stamps?

definitions.definition: to run fast in order to get or avoid something
definitions.example: I ran for the bus but it drove off.

definitions.definition: to move your legs as if running, while you stay in one place
definitions.example: I run on the spot to warm up before I start training.

definitions.definition: in American football, to carry the ball towards the opponent's goal
definitions.example: It might be better to run the ball more against this defence instead of trying to pass it.

definitions.definition: to (cause something to) travel, move, or continue in a particular way
definitions.example: Trains are still running, despite the snow.

definitions.definition: to (cause something to) operate
definitions.example: Keep clear of the machines while they're running.

definitions.definition: to be in control of something
definitions.example: He's been running a restaurant/his own company since he left school.

definitions.definition: to control a business or other organization firmly and effectively
definitions.example: Ruth runs a tight ship and has no time for shirkers.

definitions.definition: If you run a car, you own one, drive it, and pay for the costs
definitions.example: I can't afford to run a car.

definitions.definition: to organize the way you live or work
definitions.example: Some people run their lives according to the movements of the stars.

definitions.definition: to (cause something to) flow or produce liquid
definitions.example: run down I can feel trickles of sweat running down my neck.

definitions.definition: (of colours in clothes, etc.) to come out or spread
definitions.example: I must have washed my dress at too high a temperature, because the colour has run.

definitions.definition: to be or become
definitions.example: run deep Differences between the two sides run deep (= are serious).

definitions.definition: If tights (= thin clothing that covers the legs) run, a long, thin hole appears in them
definitions.example: Oh no, my tights have run!

definitions.definition: to show something in a newspaper or magazine, on television, etc.
definitions.example: All the newspapers ran (= printed) stories about the new peace talks.

definitions.definition: to appear in a newspaper, magazine, etc. or to be shown on television
definitions.example: The story orginally ran in the December 4th issue of the newspaper.

definitions.definition: If a film is running at a particular place, you can see it there
definitions.example: What's running at the Metro this week?

definitions.definition: to compete as a candidate in an election
definitions.example: Mrs Thatcher wanted to run a fourth time.

definitions.definition: to suggest and support someone as a candidate (= someone competing to get a job or elected position)
definitions.example: run someone for something He wanted to run her for district attorney of Brooklyn.

definitions.definition: to compete as a candidate in an election for a position of authority and responsibility in a government or other organization
definitions.example: She is considering running for office.

definitions.definition: to take guns or drugs illegally from one place to another
definitions.example: run something across something He was arrested for running drugs across the border.

definitions.definition: to cost someone a particular amount of money
definitions.example: A taxi across town will run you a few dollars.

definitions.definition: to give something to someone
definitions.example: The manager ran me a few free goods to make up the difference.

definitions.definition: the action of running, especially for exercise
definitions.example: go for a run We go for a three-mile run every evening after work.

definitions.definition: a journey
definitions.example: The number of aircraft on the New York-Moscow run is being increased.

definitions.definition: the period during which a play is performed
definitions.example: The musical's London run was a disaster.

definitions.definition: a situation in which many people suddenly buy a particular product
definitions.example: run on There's been a run on umbrellas because of all this rain.

definitions.definition: a situation in which many people suddenly sell a particular product
definitions.example: run on A sudden run on the dollar has lowered its value.

definitions.definition: A run of something is a continuous period during which it lasts or is repeated
definitions.example: a run of successes/defeats/bad luck

definitions.definition: a series of notes of a scale played or sung quickly one after the other
definitions.example: The singer's vocal runs sounded effortless.

definitions.definition: the usual type of something
definitions.example: Their food is the general run of hotel cooking.

definitions.definition: an area of ground of limited size for keeping animals
definitions.example: a sheep/chicken/hen run

definitions.definition: in cricket and baseball, a single point, scored by running from one place to another
definitions.example: England need 105 runs to win the game.

definitions.definition: a long, vertical hole in tights and stockings
definitions.example: I've got a run in my tights from the nail on my chair.

definitions.definition: a condition of the bowels in which the contents are passed out of the body too often and in a form that is too liquid
to move your legs faster than when walking, with the weight of your body pressing forward
definitions.example: [ I ] They ran for the bus and got there just in time.

definitions.definition: to travel or go, to move something, or to be positioned in a particular way
definitions.example: [ I ] The bus runs three times a day between here and Albuquerque.

definitions.definition: If you run your finger or hand over something, you move it quickly
definitions.example: [ T ] She ran her fingers along the edge of the desk.

definitions.definition: If you run something through your hair, you move it quickly and easily
definitions.example: [ T ] He ran a comb through his hair.

definitions.definition: If a driver or a vehicle runs a sign or signal to stop, the vehicle continues without stopping
definitions.example: [ T ] Our taxi ran a red light and a truck rammed us in the side.

definitions.definition: to manage or operate something
definitions.example: [ T ] She runs the business out of her home.

definitions.definition: If something runs on a particular type of energy, it uses that type of energy to operate
definitions.example: [ I ] Some calculators run on solar power .

definitions.definition: to cause a liquid to flow, or to produce a liquid that flows
definitions.example: [ T ] He ran a little cold water into the sink.

definitions.definition: (of colors) to come out of material and mix with other colors, so that the original colors are lost
definitions.example: If you wash the dress in hot water, the colors will run.

definitions.definition: to try to get elected; be a candidate
definitions.example: Kutukas ran unsuccessfully for sheriff.

definitions.definition: to be, become, or continue in a particular way
definitions.example: [ L ] The doctor is running a bit late.

definitions.definition: to show something in a newspaper or magazine, or on television
definitions.example: Both parties are already running campaign ads.

definitions.definition: (of cloth, esp. stockings (= thin, tight-fitting clothing for a woman’s feet and legs)) to develop a long vertical hole
definitions.example: My stockings ran!

definitions.definition: (in baseball) a single point, scored by touching each of the four bases (= positions on a square) in the correct order
a long, vertical hole in particular types of cloth, esp. stockings (= thin, tight-fitting clothing for a woman’s feet and legs)
a trip
definitions.example: The train made its final run in 1986.

definitions.definition: a period during which something happens or continues
definitions.example: The movie starts a two-week run tonight.

definitions.definition: to operate, or make something operate
definitions.example: Keep clear of the fans while they're running.

definitions.definition: to be in control of or manage something
definitions.example: He's been running his own company since he left school.

definitions.definition: to travel or move in a particular way, or cause something to do this
definitions.example: Trains are still running, despite the snow.

definitions.definition: to continue or happen, or cause something to continue or happen in a particular way
definitions.example: A magazine subscription usually runs for one year.

definitions.definition: to take something to a person or place
definitions.example: run sth over/out/down, etc. to sb/sth Can you run these orders over to the warehouse, please?

definitions.definition: to be or continue at or near a particular level
definitions.example: run at sth Inflation has been running at 2% for the past year.

definitions.definition: to show something in a newspaper or magazine, on television, etc.
definitions.example: run a story/article/piece

definitions.definition: to try to be elected to government or other position in an election
definitions.example: run for sth He ran for state Attorney General in 2010.

definitions.definition: to look through records to find out facts about someone or something
definitions.example: We run background checks on all prospective employees.

definitions.definition: to perform a scientific examination to determine if something works, someone is healthy, etc.
definitions.example: We ran performance tests on the preproduction machine, which performed well.

definitions.definition: if a government runs a deficit or surplus, it has less or more money in its accounts than it needs
definitions.example: The previous government was happy to run a huge deficit for years.

definitions.definition: to be in a situation in which there is the possibility that something bad might happen
definitions.example: A company without good customer service runs the risk of losing its customers' good will.

definitions.definition: to control a business or other organization firmly and effectively
definitions.example: The woman who manages the post room runs a very tight ship.

definitions.definition: to look quickly at the whole of something
definitions.example: Would you mind running your eye over this agreement before I sign it?

definitions.definition: to be unable to get to a place by the agreed or expected time
to be very active without achieving any good results
definitions.example: Peter's been running round in circles since half his department resigned.

definitions.definition: to have no time left to finish something or get to a place
definitions.example: We're running out of time - the report has to be ready for the meeting tonight.

definitions.definition: to have a low supply of something
definitions.example: Forecasting is crucial: you don't want to run short or have a warehouse of unsold product.

definitions.definition: to do calculations in order to decide whether a particular plan is financially practical
definitions.example: She ran the numbers and decided to re-finance her mortgage.

definitions.definition: to examine something to see if it is good enough or right for a particular purpose
definitions.example: A number of bidders are understood to be running the rule over the company.

definitions.definition: to be the leader in control of a group of people doing something
definitions.example: If you need help, ask Mark - he's running the show.

definitions.definition: all of a particular product made at one time
definitions.example: The first run of 50,000 units sold out in a week.

definitions.definition: a period when a series of good things or bad things happen
definitions.example: a run of good/bad luck We've had quite a run of good luck this month.

definitions.definition: a period when people buy more of a particular product than usual
definitions.example: The warm weather sparked a run on air conditioners.

definitions.definition: a period when many people suddenly sell more of a particular currency than usual
definitions.example: a run on the dollar/pound/yen A sudden run on the dollar has lowered its value.

definitions.definition: a period when many people take their money out of a bank because they are afraid the bank will go out of business
definitions.example: A run on the bank by customers drained about $133 million.
